operator_path: Install the exact frozen Python 3.12 environment once, then generate the committed JSON Schemas, the OpenAPI document, and the compatibility registry deterministically from the versioned Pydantic authoring source and run the full canonical checks offline on Windows and Linux without credentials or public network.
must_scope: Add pydantic>=2,<3, jsonschema>=4,<5, and rfc8785==0.1.4 to the existing dev dependency group only and freeze the full resolution in uv.lock; [project].dependencies stays empty; the dependency-family decision is bound by ADR-0026 accepted in this planning change

Author all 14 bootstrap contracts as versioned Pydantic v2 authoring types under src/hermes_pipeline/contracts/: 13 root contracts plus the common/definitions $defs type library; every model config sets extra="forbid" explicitly and preserves the f36 Draft 2020-12 pass/reject boundary: no string, boolean, or incompatible-primitive coercion, but integer fields accept finite integral JSON numeric values such as 3.0 whenever the Schema accepts them

Deterministically generate and commit, from that single authoring source, the 14 JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 documents under schemas/, the OpenAPI document at contracts/openapi.json, and the compatibility registry at contracts/compatibility-registry.json; generation is pure, order-stable, LF/UTF-8, and contains no timestamp, path, or environment input

Perform a one-time reviewed representation-only migration: every generated Schema keeps its exact $id and Draft 2020-12 declaration, the 14-Schema identity lock is unchanged, and no existing JSON document schema_id is edited

Prove /v1 semantic equivalence against an immutable, committed snapshot of the exact f36ba6a Schemas: tests/fixtures/contracts/ contains the snapshots and raw-digest manifest as historical evidence, not a second authoring source; the baseline validator builds its complete $ref registry only from the 14 raw-digested snapshots; every baseline corpus entry is first validated by that precise baseline Schema, then by the strict Pydantic model and generated Schema, and all pass/reject results must agree; digest labels alone are not evidence

Implement RFC 8785 canonical JSON and content hashing with rfc8785 as the single JCS implementation: content_hash computed with the content_hash field absent, UTF-8 SHA-256, committed golden vectors, and rejection of NaN, Infinity, and lone surrogates; no sort_keys approximation

Add per-root-contract minimal, maximal, invalid, legacy-compatibility, and secret-canary instance corpora for the 13 instantiable root contracts plus per-$defs fragment tests for common/definitions; canaries never appear in errors, logs, reports, or CLI output

Add a finite compatibility-range registry committed at contracts/compatibility-registry.json and a pure migration Interface with no storage, business state, or real migration; migration verifies document.schema_id and schema_version against the requested supported identity before recording that original schema identity and migrated digest

Generate the OpenAPI 3.1.0 document with fixed openapi 3.1.0, jsonSchemaDialect set to Draft 2020-12, non-empty info, explicit empty paths, and components.schemas whose 14 component values fully embed the corresponding generated Schema including its exact $id, under keys mapping exactly one-to-one to the 14 registry $ids by the rule PascalCase(namespace) + PascalCase(resource) + V + version; external $ref substitutes and placeholders are forbidden; the full 14-entry mapping is fixed in AC-07

Upgrade the contracts check command to the full validator while scripts/check_schemas.py remains the untouched dependency-free bootstrap gate, and add a consistency test aligning both validators on the 14-Schema registry

Keep contracts generate as a development-only write command; contracts drift-check writes every generated artifact under a TemporaryDirectory and compares the exact generated file set and bytes read-only against the committed files

Dispatch the contract toolchain lazily: the Hermes plugin entry, --version, and the normal runtime path remain pure standard library; pydantic, jsonschema, and rfc8785 are imported only after the contracts subcommand is parsed, and every contracts failure path returns bounded, control-character-sanitized output without leaking canaries or tracebacks

Extend python-quality.yml with the new offline checks, including the exact uv run --offline python -m hermes_pipeline.cli contracts drift-check command, and update the frozen command inventory inside scripts/check_documentation.py and its workflow fixtures so --check-workflows accepts the extended workflow; documentation-contracts.yml and check_schemas.py remain unchanged

Recompute content_hash values only for the 00-03 generated artifacts and the files explicitly listed in permitted_paths; recomputing content_hash in historical planning, review, evidence, or closeout records requires a Contract Change Request
Keep README.md, docs/README.md, schemas/README.md, and CONTRIBUTING.md accurate for the upgraded contracts check semantics and the adopted authoring source
Record the added dev-only toolchain, its exact version locks, and the compatibility evidence in docs/development/compatibility-targets.md

Prove platform reproducibility: generation and all checks are byte-identical on Windows and Linux with LF endings and no cache or bytecode residue; final verification inherits PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1

interfaces: Pydantic v2 authoring types in src/hermes_pipeline/contracts/ (13 root contracts plus the common/definitions $defs type library) as the sole source of schemas/, contracts/openapi.json, and contracts/compatibility-registry.json; strict model validation preserves the f36 Schema pass/reject boundary, including coercion-sensitive cases such as integral 3.0 JSON numbers for integer Schema fields; an explicit divergence allowlist is forbidden

contracts check: full read-only validation with Slice 00-02 exit semantics (0 pass, 1 fail), gaining meta-validation, corpus, and canonical-hash coverage; the command name is unchanged and the toolchain is lazy-imported only after the contracts subcommand is parsed

OpenAPI component keys: for every $id https://schemas.hermes-pipeline.dev/{namespace}/{resource}/v{n}, the component key is PascalCase(namespace) + PascalCase(resource) + V + n; the 14 fixed mappings are enumerated in AC-07

Compatibility registry structure: a JSON object mapping each registry $id to {current_version: integer >= 1, supported_versions: non-empty strictly increasing integer array with current_version as its maximum}; the key set must equal the 14-Schema $id set exactly

Validation parity: register a deterministic RFC 3339 date-time checker on Draft202012Validator.FORMAT_CHECKER using the same shared rule as the authoring type, because the frozen jsonschema installation omits the optional checker; do not add a dependency family or accept a Schema/model divergence

acceptance_criteria.observable_result: All 14 committed Schemas are deterministic Pydantic-authoring outputs; each keeps its exact $id and Draft 2020-12 declaration; the 14-Schema identity lock is unchanged. The new canonical projection need not be byte-equal to f36, and no f36-layout compatibility table or byte-equality assertion is permitted.

contracts drift-check writes the complete generated artifact set into a temporary directory and byte-compares the exact file set read-only with the committed files; output is byte-identical on Windows and Linux with LF, UTF-8, and no timestamps or paths.

Every generated Schema passes Draft202012Validator.check_schema meta-validation, $ref closure resolution across the registry, and instance validation with Draft202012Validator.FORMAT_CHECKER enabled; the frozen environment registers the deterministic RFC 3339 date-time checker, so a format-violating instance is rejected by both Schema validation and the authoring model.

The 13 instantiable root contracts each have committed minimal, maximal, invalid, legacy-compatibility, and secret-canary instance corpora; common/definitions has per-$defs fragment tests instead of instance corpora; valid entries pass and invalid entries are rejected deterministically, and canaries never leak.

Every baseline corpus entry is first validated by the immutable f36 Schema snapshot through a snapshot-only $ref registry with the expected pass or reject result recorded, then validated by the Pydantic model and generated Schema; all three results agree, including coercion-sensitive cases. Integer Schema fields accept finite integral JSON numbers such as 3.0 but reject strings, booleans, and non-integral numbers. Positive entries additionally pass Model validate, JSON dump, then Model and Schema revalidate; no semantic change, divergence allowlist, or /v2 jump occurs.

RFC 8785 canonicalization via the pinned rfc8785 package matches committed golden vectors; content_hash is computed with the content_hash field absent; NaN, Infinity, and lone surrogates are rejected.

The committed contracts/openapi.json is fixed 3.1.0 with jsonSchemaDialect Draft 2020-12, non-empty info, explicit empty paths, and exactly these 14 component keys mapping one-to-one to the registry $ids: CommonDefinitionsV1, EngineeringCloseoutV1, EngineeringContextManifestV1, EngineeringContractChangeRequestV1, EngineeringExecutionReportV1, EngineeringPhasePlanV1, EngineeringReviewVerdictV1, EngineeringSliceContractV1, RuntimeArtifactManifestV1, RuntimeCapabilityProfileV1, RuntimeCommandReceiptV1, RuntimeControllerCommandV1, RuntimeEvidenceBundleV1, RuntimePipelineEventV1; each component fully embeds the matching generated Schema including its exact $id, with no external $ref substitute; no servers, operationId, or security placeholders.

The committed contracts/compatibility-registry.json maps each of the 14 registry $ids to {current_version: integer >= 1, supported_versions: non-empty strictly increasing integer array with current_version as its maximum}; the key set equals the $id set exactly; the migration Interface is pure with no storage or business state, rejects a requested identity that differs from document.schema_id or an unsupported source version, and records the verified original schema identity and migrated digest.

Upgraded contracts check and the untouched bootstrap gate agree on the 14-Schema registry; python-quality.yml steps match the frozen command inventory of scripts/check_documentation.py --check-workflows, including the exact offline contracts drift-check command; the full canonical command set passes on Windows and Linux offline after installation; git diff --check is clean.

pydantic, jsonschema, and rfc8785 are imported only after the contracts subcommand is parsed; the Hermes plugin entry, --version, and the normal runtime path never import them; every contracts failure path, including malformed Schema registry input, returns a bounded UTF-8-byte-limited, control-character-sanitized error without tracebacks or canaries; verification leaves no cache or bytecode artifact.

risks.description: Pydantic generation or validation can silently change a bootstrap constraint or diverge from Draft 2020-12 numeric and format semantics, breaking agreement with the immutable f36 Schema snapshots.
risks.mitigation: Commit raw-digested f36 Schema snapshots, build their registry independently, register the deterministic date-time checker, cover integral numeric and format boundaries, and require agreement among the baseline Schema, Pydantic model, and generated Schema as a regression gate.
risks.trigger: A baseline entry result differs among the f36 Schema snapshot, strict model, and generated Schema.

risks.description: RFC 8785 edge cases (numbers, Unicode ordering, control characters, surrogates) diverge from the reference implementation.
risks.mitigation: Pin rfc8785==0.1.4 as the single JCS implementation and commit official-style golden vectors.
risks.trigger: A golden vector fails or a second canonicalization implementation appears.

risks.description: The OpenAPI component set drifts from the Schema registry or gains HTTP placeholders.
risks.mitigation: Enforce the fixed 14-entry component key to $id mapping, full canonical equality with generated Schema objects, and empty paths in contracts check and drift.
risks.trigger: A component is added, removed, renamed, replaced by an external ref/placeholder, differs from its generated Schema, or paths is non-empty.

risks.description: The full validator and the bootstrap gate disagree on registry integrity, or the extended workflow violates the frozen command inventory.
risks.mitigation: Add a consistency test running both validators over the same registry and update the frozen command inventory with the exact offline drift-check workflow command.
risks.trigger: The two validators reach different conclusions, the offline drift-check is absent/altered, or --check-workflows rejects the extended workflow.

risks.description: Generation or validation output differs between Windows and Linux.
risks.mitigation: Pure generation with LF and UTF-8 output, no timestamps or paths, and identical commands on both required systems.
risks.trigger: drift-check differs between platforms or from the committed files.

risks.description: A runtime entry path imports a contract-toolchain package before the contracts subcommand is parsed, breaking the standard-library-only rule.
risks.mitigation: Lazy-dispatch the toolchain after subcommand parsing and add an import-boundary regression test; contracts reports a bounded error without development dependencies.
risks.trigger: The Hermes plugin entry, --version, or the normal runtime path imports pydantic, jsonschema, or rfc8785.

stop_conditions: A dependency family beyond ADR-0026, FastAPI, or any service framework is required
Runtime dependencies must change or contract-toolchain packages must be imported before the contracts subcommand is parsed

A baseline entry result still differs among the immutable f36 Schema snapshot, Pydantic model, and generated Schema after applying the required date-time checker and Draft 2020-12 integral-number semantics; the replacement stops and a Contract Change Request is submitted without silently changing semantics, accepting a divergence allowlist, or jumping to /v2
Any $id changes, a Schema is added or removed, or the identity lock must be altered
Generation output differs between Windows and Linux or from the committed files
A golden vector fails or a second canonicalization implementation is required
A secret canary leaks, verification leaves cache or bytecode artifacts, or a required check needs credentials, public network after installation, or shell-string execution
The OpenAPI document must deviate from fixed 3.1.0, jsonSchemaDialect Draft 2020-12, empty paths, the fixed 14-entry component mapping, or full embedded canonical equality with generated Schemas
The compatibility registry cannot validate structurally or its key set cannot equal the registry $id set
Recomputing content_hash in historical planning, review, evidence, or closeout records becomes necessary

Implementation requires paths outside permitted_paths or changes check_schemas.py, check_repository_artifacts.py, documentation-contracts.yml, .gitattributes, accepted ADRs, or planning, review, evidence, and closeout records
The Base SHA changes or required Windows and Linux behavior cannot be equivalent
